style_when: the article describes one decisive moment or place — a yard at dawn, a control room, a shutdown line, a handover — that a film still could hold
prompt: Cinematic film still, 35mm anamorphic wide, low camera angle: a dark, empty control room at night, its concrete floor catching green light. The hero is a wall-mounted release status board — a large grid of small glass indicator lamps set in perforated brushed steel, every lamp glowing the same deep pine green. The board hangs high and off-centre right, its light raking down across a vacant operator console in graphite and steel blue, while deep shadow and generous negative space fill the lower left. A faint cool doorway light leaks in from far left. Deep focus, crisp atmospheric depth, restrained green-on-graphite palette, fine film grain, no people, no text, no logos.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, numbers, watermarks, logos
rationale: The story turns on one decisive place and artifact — the green board the article says it would not trust — and a cinematic still can hold that quiet moment of false confidence. A dark, empty control room lit only by an all-green status wall makes the blindness physical: nothing in the frame looks wrong, which is precisely the finding.
subject: a wall-mounted grid of green indicator lamps — the all-green release status board — hanging over a vacant operator console in a dark control room
core_thesis: A coding agent's skill layer is a stateful supply chain in which a co-installed look-alike skill can silently displace the installed one and drop its rules, while the green task-completion tests keep approving the run.
core_conflict: The green release gate versus the invisible hijack: task completion stays green while guardrails are dropped and artifacts carry attacks into later sessions.
composition: Low-angle anamorphic wide; the green board commands the upper right two-thirds of the frame, with deep shadow and generous negative space across the lower left
